content.overview: BNS s. 347 — Counterfeiting a property mark.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Counterfeiting a property mark. BNS restatement of IPC 483. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 483. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 347 is the rule on “Counterfeiting a property mark”. The section provides that ( 1) Whoever counterfeits any property mark used by any other person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 347 exists so that “Counterfeiting a property mark” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: False documents, forgery, using a forged electronic record, property marks.

The provision in detail
347.( 1) Whoever counterfeits any property mark used by any other person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

(2) Whoever counterfeits any property mark used by a public servant, or any mark used by a public servant to denote that any property has been manufactured by a particular person or at a particular time or place, or that the property is of a particular quality or has passed through a particular office, or that it is entitled to any exemption, or uses as genuine any such mark knowing the same to be counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. ( 1) Whoever counterfeits any property mark used by any other person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
2. (2) Whoever counterfeits any property mark used by a public servant, or any mark used by a public servant to denote that any property has been manufactured by a particular person or at a particular time or place, or that the property is of a particular quality or has passed through a particular office, or that it is entitled to any exemption, or uses as genuine any such mark knowing the same to be counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 347 (Counterfeiting a property mark) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 347 (Counterfeiting a property mark), Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever counterfeits any property mark used by any other person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
   (2) Whoever counterfeits any property mark used by a public servant, or any mark used by a public servant to denote that any property has been manufactured by a particular person or at a particular time or place, or that the property is of a particular quality or has passed through a particular office, or that it is entitled to any exemption, or uses as genuine any such mark knowing the same to be counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 347 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 347 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 347 constitutes a key component of Chapter XVIII (Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing counterfeiting a property mark. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of counterfeiting a property mark under Section 347 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 347.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 347 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 347 vs General Attempt: Section 347 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XVIII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 347 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 347 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 347 for conduct relating to counterfeiting a property mark.
Rule: Under BNS s. 347, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 347.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 347 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
